Long-lived assets held and used are assessed for possible impairment by comparing their carrying values with their associated undiscounted, future cash flows. LivaNova allocates any excess purchase price over the fair value of the net tangible and identifiable intangible assets acquired to goodwill. LivaNova bases the fair value of identifiable intangible assets acquired in a business combination, including IPR&D, on valuations that use information and assumptions provided by management, which consider management’s best estimates of inputs and assumptions that a market participant would use.

capex.text: Each reporting period, LivaNova determines whether there are circumstances that warrant an evaluation of the carrying amounts of LivaNova’s property and equipment and its finite-lived intangible assets to determine whether such carrying amounts continue to be recoverable. Such changes in circumstance may include, among other items, an expectation of a sale or disposal of a long-lived asset or asset group, adverse changes in market or competitive conditions, an adverse change in legal factors or business climate in the markets in which LivaNova operates, and operating or cash flow losses. Long-lived assets held and used are assessed for possible impairment by comparing their carrying values with their associated undiscounted, future cash flows. In order to calculate the impairment charge, LivaNova generally measures fair value by considering sale prices for similar assets, discounted estimated future cash flows using an appropriate discount rate, and/or estimated replacement cost.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales consists primarily of direct labor, allocated manufacturing overhead, and the acquisition of raw materials and components.

Cost of sales as a percentage of net revenue was 32.3% for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing an increase of 0.4 percentage points compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to unfavorable product mix, partially offset by a decrease in cost of sales from the winding down of the ACS segment.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expense
rd.text:
R&D expenses consist of product design and development efforts, clinical study programs, and regulatory activities.

R&D expenses as a percentage of net revenue were 13.4% for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing a decrease of 1.2 percentage points compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. The decrease was primarily due to reductions in costs associated with the Company’s DTD program of $18.9 million, partially offset by an $11.2 million increase in costs associated with the development of LivaNova’s aura6000 System for treating OSA.

other_opex.heading: Other Operating Expense
other_opex.text:
Other operating expense consists of the provision for litigation involving LivaNova’s 3T Heater-Cooler device, the Saluggia site remediation provision, and restructuring expense.

Other operating expense as a percentage of net revenue was 0.4% for the year ended December 31, 2025, a decrease of 2.2 percentage points compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in the amount recorded for the litigation provision related to LivaNova’s 3T Heater-Cooler device of $15.3 million, as well as a decrease in restructuring expense of $13.5 million. For additional information, refer to “Note 11. Commitments and Contingencies” and “Note 4. Restructuring” in the consolidated financial statements in this Report.

nonop.text: LivaNova incurred interest expense of $49.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $63.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
LivaNova is a UK corporation and operates through the Company’s various subsidiaries in a number of countries throughout the world. LivaNova’s provision for income taxes is based on the tax laws and rates applicable in the jurisdictions in which the Company operates and earns income. LivaNova uses significant judgment and estimates in accounting for the Company’s income taxes. The Company recognizes deferred tax assets and liabilities for the anticipated future tax effects of temporary differences between the financial statements basis and the tax basis of LivaNova’s assets and liabilities, which are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.

LivaNova files national and local tax returns in many jurisdictions throughout the world and is subject to income tax examinations for its fiscal year 2020 and subsequent years, with certain exceptions. While LivaNova believes that its tax return positions are fully supported, tax authorities may disagree with certain positions the Company has taken and assess additional taxes, and, as a result, LivaNova may establish reserves for uncertain tax positions, which require a significant degree of management judgment.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
